title: Grounded Theory
short_description: Guidance for iterative coding, constant comparison, memo-writing, category development, and theoretical integration.

phases.title: Initial/open coding
phases.description: Stay close to the data and code actions, processes, and meanings.
prompts: Can this code be phrased actively?

phases.title: Constant comparison
phases.description: Compare incident with incident, code with code, and category with category.

phases.title: Focused coding
phases.description: Select the most useful or frequent codes for more systematic analysis.
prompts: Which codes should be merged or split?
recommended_actions: Promote promising codes into axial codes.

phases.title: Axial coding
phases.description: Relate codes through conditions, context, action/interaction, and consequences.
prompts: What actions or interactions respond to it?
recommended_actions: Link open codes to axial codes.

phases.title: Category development
phases.description: Develop categories with explanatory power and clear relationships to supporting codes.
prompts: What negative cases test this category?

phases.title: Theoretical integration
phases.description: Integrate categories into a coherent analytical explanation.

phases.title: Memo-writing
phases.description: Use memos to elaborate codes, categories, comparisons, and theoretical decisions.
recommended_actions: Link memos to codes and segments.

phases.title: Saturation/refinement
phases.description: Refine categories by checking whether new data adds important properties, dimensions, or contradictions.
prompts: Does this add a new property?
What comparison should be made next?
What category does this evidence strengthen?

concepts.description: The iterative practice of comparing data, codes, and categories to refine concepts.
A memo that develops conceptual relationships rather than only describing data.

sources.apa: Charmaz, K. (2014). Constructing grounded theory (2nd ed.). SAGE.
sources.note: Use for initial coding, focused coding, memo-writing, and constructivist GT.

sources.apa: Strauss, A., & Corbin, J. (1998). Basics of qualitative research: Techniques and procedures for developing grounded theory (2nd ed.). SAGE.
sources.note: Use for axial coding, categories, properties, dimensions, and theoretical integration.

sources.apa: Clarke, A. E. (2005). Situational analysis: Grounded theory after the postmodern turn. SAGE.
sources.note: Use for situational mapping and extending GT toward discourse and social worlds.
